headlines.article_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu watch now VIDEO 4:13 04:13 Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns immediately Squawk Box Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down as CEO of the chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago and built into a $4 trillion company that powered the artificial intelligence boom, the company announced Thursday. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. "The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," said board chair Harvey Jones in a release announcing the news. The company will begin the search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang and will consider both internal and external candidates, according to the release. Kress also provided a statement in the release, but Huang was not quoted. After a meteoric rise to fame due to Nvidia's central role in AI, Huang's dramatic fall has been even more rapid, following a series of stinging revelations about his romantic ties to a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy. Huang, 63, apologized on Sunday for being "unfaithful to my wife," though he provided no details about the affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, who has worked for a Chinese company and Nvidia customer called Megaspeed. Late Wednesday, The New York Times reported that the Nvidia CEO also had a separate affair, this one with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at the chipmaker. Later that afternoon, The Times and other outlets reported that Nvidia's board met to discuss the company's future. Huang's downfall also puts the spotlight on President Donald Trump , who formed a particularly close relationship with the CEO of what, until recently, was the world's most valuable company. Huang became a key voice on U.S. AI policy while pushing for issues that were in Nvidia's interest, such as preserving access to open-source AI, and lobbying to allow chip exports to China. Pete Kiehart | Bloomberg | Getty Images Senate Majority Leader John Thune , R-S.D., said he expects Congress to conduct oversight of the Jensen Huang affair even after the embattled tech CEO's resignation. "In this environment where there's some really high stakes when it comes to our national security, I would expect there would be some follow-up, yeah," Thune said when asked by reporters if there would be congressional investigations into the matter. Thune earlier this week was reelected Senate Republican leader. The GOP will be in the minority come January, after Democrats won at least 55 seats in the upper chamber. — Garrett Downs 9 Min Ago Hugging Face CEO on Huang ouster: 'A really sad day' Clement Delangue, co-founder and chief executive officer of Hugging Face Inc., during the Bloomberg Technology Summit in San Francisco, California, US, on Thursday, May 9, 2024. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue lamented Huang's ouster from Nvidia, writing in a LinkedIn post that it's "a really sad day." Nvidia in September agreed to acquire Hugging Face, a leading platform for open-source AI models, in a deal worth about $12.9 billion . The company expects the deal to close in the first half of 2027. "This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened," Delangue wrote. "It's a really sad day!" He continued, "But I want to make one thing clear: we'll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let's go!" The Hugging Face deal, which is the second-largest in Nvidia's history, has attracted scrutiny from regulators. CNBC previously reported that the U.S. Department of Justice is probing the acquisition and how it could impact competition in the AI market. — Annie Palmer 11 Min Ago Mast still has confidence in Lutnick, wants BIS investigated Howard Lutnick, US commerce secretary, during an executive order signing in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Tuesday, March 31, 2026. Aaron Schwartz | Bloomberg | Getty Images House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast, R-Fla., told reporters on Thursday that he still has confidence in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick despite reporting this week that he stalled President Donald Trump' s crackdowns on firms routing Nvidia chips to China . Mast also said he wanted Congress to investigate the role of the Bureau of Industry and Security, a subagency of the Commerce Department that manages and enforces export controls, in the Huang scandal. The New York Times reported earlier this week that the company's general counsel, Tim Teter, claimed in emails to commerce investigators looking into Alice Huang's company that he'd been in touch with Jeffrey Kessler, who leads BIS. The commerce investigation into Haung's company, Megaspeed, was then transferred to the Justice Department. "The people that we deal with in BIS, those are the ones that are at the granular level of dealing with Nvidia and chips," Mast said. Mast said he hadn't spoken to Lutnick or Kessler since the revelations. — Justin Papp 14 Min Ago Creative Strategies CEO Ben Bajarin: Huang was a 'trendsetter' for semiconductor industry watch now VIDEO 4:42 04:42 Huang was a 'trendsetter for the industry': Creative Strategies CEO Ben Bajarin Squawk on the Street Creative Strategies CEO Ben Bajarin called Huang a "trendsetter" and said his exit creates "a huge shakeup and an impact to the industry." "Anytime ... you lose a founder-level-type of charisma who really has been looked upon as the, this trendsetter for the industry, the spokesperson for this moment that we have in this technology build out, that's going to be a loss," Bajarin told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" Thursday. Uncertainty over who will ultimately take the helm at Nvidia only adds to the challenge, according to the Creative Strategies CEO. Bajarin sees VP of Nvidia's data center business Ian Buck as the most logical candidate to be Huang's permanent replacement, with an internal pick likely preferable to an external candidate. "You have to have deep semiconductor expertise ... it's a very short list of people who can do that at this scale." "What they need to bring back is somebody who can normalize things and be that type of person who can keep the troops aligned, keep them convicted on what they're doing in their engineering, and preserve that culture," Bajarin said. — Caleigh Keating 22 Min Ago Nvidia stock is now pricing in a ‘leadership discount,’ says Landsberg Jensen Huang, chief executive officer of Nvidia Corp., speaks to members of the media following the company's "Japan AI Ecosystem" reception in Tokyo, Japan, on Thursday, July 16, 2026. headlines.summary: Cosm has secured a new studio partnership with Disney that will bring "Star Wars: A New Hope" to its domes as part of a multiyear, multifilm collaboration.
headlines.article_text: 'Star Wars' is coming to Cosm domes ahead of 50th anniversary Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Cosm has partnered with Disney on a multiyear, multifilm deal that will kick off with "Star Wars: A New Hope" early next year. This is Cosm's third studio deal — it already has partnerships with Universal and Warner Bros. — and sixth theatrical release. Cosm is working directly with studios Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic as well as creative studio MakeMake to create the visuals and the sound mixing for a unique presentation of the film. In this article DIS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A poster for Disney and Lucasfilm's "Star Wars: A New Hope" in shared reality at Cosm. Cosm The Force is strong with Cosm. On Thursday, the immersive entertainment technology company announced a new studio partnership with The Walt Disney Company that will bring the original "Star Wars" to its domes early next year as part of a multiyear, multifilm collaboration. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. Cosm's massive concave screens will drop film fans into a galaxy far, far away starting in March, just ahead of the Academy Award-winning film's 50th anniversary in May. "We are thrilled to add the Disney partnership," Alexis Scalice, head of Cosm Studios, told CNBC. "We do look for those opportunities of these like anniversary and commemorative moments. We look for those opportunities to celebrate with the fans, but also find this mutually beneficial partnership between both parties." This will be Cosm's sixth theatrical collaboration with Hollywood, having already partnered with Warner Bros. to bring "The Matrix," "Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory," "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" and "It" to its locations. The company is set to launch immersive screenings of Universal's "Shrek" in December. Each Cosm dome has stadium-style seating, with booths and tables set on each level. The dome's width fills much of the viewers' periphery, giving the sensation that they are part of the onscreen environment. Cosm's LA venue playing "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" in shared reality. Courtesy of Cosm In this case, "Star Wars" will be displayed in a large rectangle in the center of the dome while the background is transformed into the iconic planets of Tatooine and Yavin IV that are featured in the film as well as the infamous Death Star. Audiences will also see elements that will make it appear like they're traveling at lightspeed and getting trapped in an intergalactic trash compactor. Cosm is working directly with studios Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic as well as creative studio MakeMake to create the visuals and the sound mixing for the unique presentation of the film. "We look for those moments where sound, music ... listening to Darth Vader's breath for the first time ... you feel those moments differently in an 87-foot diameter dome and 12k resolution with the sound system we have," Scalice said. "And it's one of the things that with experiential cinema and our technology that we were so excited and honestly privileged that we can take these defining moments for fans and work closely with our partners that doesn't really change the authenticity of it, it just enhances it in a different manner." The premium experience will also be paired with a themed menu. Cosm has done this with other titles, such as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone," serving guests throughout the screening with house-made shepherd's pie, pretzel wands with cheese dip and a box of Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans. Cosm is trying to establish itself as a destination for fandom — both for sports and for film. It has a wide variety of live event offerings, which it telecasts using proprietary cameras mounted in arenas that broadcast back to the dome, as well as its expanding library of movies. "What I love is that we really are kind of building these Cosm communities built on fandom," Scalice said. "It's the No. 1 foundation for our business." And Star Wars is a powerful fandom. The franchise remains one of the top-ranking pieces of intellectual property across film, television and retail annually, and Disney is gearing up for a massive celebration of its semicentennial including merchandise launches, theatrical re-releases, its biannual Star Wars Celebration convention and collaborations with other brands. headlines.article_text: Nebius Q3 earnings report 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Nebius' earnings report comes after fellow neoclouds IREN and CoreWeave showed better-than-expected results in the past week. The companies' stocks have bounced back this week after a brutal past month that reflected concerns about a slowdown in the AI buildout. Nvidia, which invests across the neocloud space, is creating added volatility due to the crisis surrounding CEO Jensen Huang. In this article NBIS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Arkady Volozh, CEO of Nebius and then Yandex CEO, speaks at the Artificial Intelligence Journey event in Moscow on Nov. 9, 2019. Mikhail Svetlov | Getty Images Nebius shares sank 16% on Thursday as one of the biggest publicly traded neoclouds reported third-quarter revenue that beat analysts' estimates, but issued disappointing guidance. Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus: Loss per share: Loss of 13 cents per share Revenue: $980.8 million vs. $907.5 million It was not immediately clear if the loss per share was comparable to the 69 cents expected by analysts. Revenue jumped 571% in the quarter, according to a statement. The company reported a net loss of $37.5 million, a loss of 13 cents per share, compared with $119.6 million, a loss of 50 cents per share, a year earlier. The stock move also comes amid the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , after stinging revelations about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia, which has developed the neocloud market by investing in the companies and backstopping some of their projects, held about $329 million in Nebius shares at the end of June, according to a filing . In a letter to shareholders , CEO Arkady Volozh said the company expects fiscal year 2026 revenue at the low end of the company's $3 billion to $3.4 billion range. FactSet expected full-year revenue of $3.35 billion. Nebius also shared an initial outlook for 2027, expecting revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, "reflecting a conservative approach to the pace of our build-out." FactSet expected 2027 revenue of $12.09 billion. The company expects FY2026 capital expenditures of $27 billion, higher than its previous capex guidance of $20 billion to $25 billion and the FactSet expectation of $23.85 billion. Nebius' expected FY2027 capex of $40 billion to $45 billion came in much higher than the FactSet expectation of $28.77 billion. Nebius stock chart.
